Valence Electron Counts

This page lists the element-specific valence electron counts stored in QTrans for each electronic-structure interface. The values follow the current definitions in src/qtrans/data/valence.py.

  • OpenMX

  • SIESTA

  • ABACUS

QTrans selects the table using basic.Ham_type and sums the counts for all atoms to determine the reference number of electrons in the unit cell. These counts are distinct from the number of atomic orbitals and from an element’s chemical valency. See Atomic Orbital Basis Definition for the orbital basis definitions. Ham_type: honpas uses the SIESTA table.

Important

Valence electron counts depend on the pseudopotential, including whether semicore states are treated as valence states. These tables document the defaults implemented in QTrans, rather than universal values for all pseudopotentials used by a given software package. Check consistency with the pseudopotentials used to generate your electronic data. Elements absent from a table have no explicit valence-count definition for that interface; their omission does not imply zero valence electrons.
